mistakes.situation: Purchasing clothing, gadgets, or accessories impulsively during flash discount sales simply because they are advertised at a discount.
mistakes.whyProblem: Discounts deceive buyers into believing they saved money, when in reality 100% of the money spent was an unplanned cash outflow for a non-essential want.
mistakes.betterAction: Enforce a mandatory 48-hour cooling period. Place the item on a wish list. If you still genuinely require it after 48 hours and have discretionary funds allocated, purchase it mindfully.

mistakes.situation: Buying daily Rs. 400 specialty drinks, canteen snacks, or ride-share trips for short walkable distances without logging them.
mistakes.whyProblem: Micro-transactions feel insignificant in isolation, but spending Rs. 600 daily accumulates to over Rs. 18,000 monthly—often exceeding a student's entire monthly savings target.
mistakes.betterAction: Set a dedicated weekly petty cash or digital wallet allowance (e.g., Rs. 2,000/week) strictly for casual daily conveniences. When the wallet balance hits zero, hold off until the next week.

mistakes.topic: Late Fee Penalties & Due Date Neglect
mistakes.situation: Postponing utility bills, hostel dues, library fines, or phone payments until after deadlines, incurring recurring late penalty surcharges.
mistakes.whyProblem: Late fees are pure deadweight loss—you forfeit money for zero return, and consistent late repayments negatively affect future financial credibility.
mistakes.betterAction: Synchronize all recurring payment dates to the first week of the month immediately following your income or stipend deposit. Enable automated calendar reminders 3 days ahead.

mistakes.situation: Signing up for 14-day free trials of streaming platforms, cloud tools, or gym tiers with credit/debit card credentials and never canceling.
mistakes.whyProblem: Companies build their business models on billing inertia. An unreviewed subscription list quietly leeches Rs. 3,000 to Rs. 7,000 each month for services you rarely open.
mistakes.betterAction: Audit your active subscription list on the 1st of every month. Adopt a 'One In, One Out' policy: never activate a new media service without canceling an existing one.

mistakes.situation: Treating your bank account balance as disposable cash and attempting to save 'whatever remains' at the end of the month.
mistakes.whyProblem: Parkinson's Law dictates that expenses naturally expand to consume all available resources. Without intentional pre-allocation, month-end remaining balance is almost always zero.
mistakes.betterAction: Execute the 'Pay Yourself First' doctrine: the moment income arrives, immediately transfer your 20% savings quota into a dedicated secondary account before spending a single rupee.
